entities.summary: Gil González Dávila was a Spanish conquistador and the first European to explore present-day Nicaragua. Born in 1480 in Ávila, Spain, Dávila began his military career as a teenager, fighting in the Battle of Navas de Tolosa. He later joined the conquistador Hernán Cortés in Mexico and participated in the conquest of the Aztec Empire. Dávila's bravery and leadership earned him a reputation as a skilled soldier, and he became known for his ability to navigate the treacherous terrain of Central America. In 1526, Dávila led an expedition to Nicaragua, which he claimed for Spain and established a Spanish settlement. His discovery marked the beginning of Spanish colonization in the region. Dávila's legacy extended beyond his military achievements, as he played a key role in the development of the Spanish Empire's expansion into the Americas. He died in 1526, but his impact on the history of Nicaragua and Central America continues to be felt today.
